name: Kegel Hold (Slow)
cues: Find the muscles: squeeze as if stopping the flow of urine and holding back gas at the same time — you should feel a lift and tightening at the base of the pelvis, behind the testicles. Do NOT clench your glutes, abs, or thighs, and keep breathing.
Lift and hold for 5 seconds (build toward 10 over weeks), breathing normally, then fully relax for the same time. The complete relaxation between reps matters as much as the squeeze.
Endurance work — builds the strength that supports erections and control. Do it sitting, standing, or lying down; daily consistency beats intensity.

name: Kegel Quick Flicks (Fast)
cues: Same lift as a slow kegel, but contract quickly and strongly, then release completely — roughly one squeeze per second.
These train the fast, reflexive control used to delay climax. Fully relax between each rep; don't recruit glutes or abs, and don't hold your breath.
Power/speed work — pair it with the slow holds.

name: Reverse Kegel (Relax & Lengthen)
cues: Instead of lifting up, gently let the pelvic floor lengthen and bulge downward — the soft feeling of beginning to pass urine or gas, or a relaxed exhale. Stay gentle, never strain or push hard.
Hold the gentle lengthening for ~5 seconds, then return to neutral.
Just as important as squeezing: an over-tight pelvic floor hurts control and stamina. Balance every kegel session with these.

name: Elevator Kegels
cues: Contract the pelvic floor in graded steps: lift a little ('floor 1'), more ('floor 2'), to a strong lift ('floor 3'), then lower step by step back to fully relaxed ('ground').
Move slowly and with control, breathing throughout. One full trip up and down = one rep.
Builds awareness and graded control — the skill behind backing off right before climax.

name: Glute Bridge + Pelvic Floor Lift
cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width. As you squeeze your glutes and lift your hips into a bridge, gently lift the pelvic floor (a kegel).
Hold at the top for 3–5 seconds with the floor engaged, then lower and fully relax everything.
Links hip and glute strength to pelvic-floor activation. Keep ribs down and breathe — don't hold your breath.

name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
cues: Lie or sit relaxed, one hand on your belly. Breathe in slowly through the nose so the belly rises and the pelvic floor naturally relaxes/descends; breathe out and let it gently recoil.
Slow, calm breaths — about 4 seconds in, 6 out. No forcing.
Down-regulates an over-tense pelvic floor and links breath to control — the same calm breathing that helps you stay relaxed and last longer.
